concepts.label: Natural-language query request (natural/natural_cred/natural_orgid/natural_context/natural_output parameters, Capella iQ-backed)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely new in Couchbase Server 8.0 and absent from the older n1ql-rest-api intro/examples set entirely: a request mode that sends an English-language prompt plus Capella credentials to the Query Service, which uses the Couchbase Capella iQ service as a backend to generate a SQL++ statement (or a CREATE FUNCTION/JS-UDF statement, or an FTS-flex-index-eligible statement), optionally auto-executing it if it is a SELECT. Kept as ONE concept for the whole 5-parameter mechanism plus its two response-side fields (generated_statement, naturalLanguageProcessingTime) rather than one concept per parameter

notable_absence.finding: This is the page the old n1ql-rest-api/intro.json record predicted would carry the credential-precedence rule ('If a request contains both HTTP basic authentication header and a creds parameter, the creds parameter is ignored and only the HTTP basic authentication header is used for authenticating') - and it does, confirming that finding. But the RBAC side stays generic here too: 'Users must have the relevant Administrative or Query & Index RBAC roles, depending on the types of query they intend to run' names no specific role, unlike n1ql-rest-functions/index.md's two named roles (Manage Global/Scope External Functions) read earlier in this same batch. The client_context_id parameter also carries a validation rule with no relation recorded for it, because no predicate in the registry models input-length/format validation: 'Maximum allowed size is 64 characters; all others will be cut. If it contains an escape character / or quote ", it will be rejected as error code 1110.'

cross_component_finding:
The natural-language query mechanism is the clearest cross-component dependency in this whole batch: a Server-side Query Service REST parameter that requires a Couchbase Capella account and credentials to function at all ('Natural language requests use the Couchbase Capella iQ service as a backend. To make a natural language request, you must have a Couchbase Capella user account.'), stated four times over (once per natural_* parameter). This means an on-premises Couchbase Server cluster's query REST API has a feature that is unusable without reaching a Capella-hosted service - the inverse of every other cross-product finding in this batch, where Server and Capella were two independent implementations of similar capabilities. No existing predicate models 'depends on a different product's cloud service to function'; dependsOnService's own registry note restricts it to service-to-service dependency within one product's architecture. I have used availableSince to record the version gate and left the Capella-iQ dependency as prose here rather than force a relation.

Secondly, the Response Body's own note - 'Additional elements not listed here might also be present. Clients and consumers of the REST API or the logs must accommodate any additional elements' - appears three times (Response Body, Controls, Metrics) and is a stated forward-compatibility contract that the schema is deliberately non-exhaustive. This directly supports the n1ql-rest-admin record's cross_component_finding that the REST envelope and the system:active_requests/completed_requests keyspaces are the same underlying data through two surfaces: if the REST schema is explicitly open-ended, a keyspace column appearing in one place and not the other is expected, not evidence against the identity.
cross_product_finding: Confirms round 10's finding that this whole REST family is Server-only, but with one asterisk: natural-language querying is the one capability on this page that is NOT Server-only in practice, because it requires a Capella account to reach the Capella iQ backend even when the query itself runs against an on-premises Server cluster. Every other request-level parameter on this page (durability_level, use_replica, use_fts, use_cbo, atrcollection, and the whole scan_consistency/scan_vector family) has a documented Capella equivalent as a request-level parameter only, per the pattern round 10 and the n1ql-rest-admin record in this batch both established: Capella exposes the same option set at the request level, with no node- or cluster-level tier. This page is where that pattern is most completely visible in one place, because unlike n1ql-rest-admin or n1ql-rest-settings, EVERY setting this page documents already has a request-level form - there is nothing here that exists at only one tier.
